newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.07 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.07 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.07 percent to close at 1.0413 per dollar in the commercial forex market after the Central Bank fixed a weaker mini-band for the currency at 1.0415 to 1.0465 per dollar, dealers said.

Some players anticipated today's lowering of the mini-band but they were surprised by the 0.14 percent decline, which was more than expected, dealers said. The market, however, remained calm following the new trade level.
The previous mini-band was set on Monday between 1.0400 and 1.0450 reais to the dollar.

Dealers said it was too early to say whether the Central Bank was speeding up the mini-band devaluation or just concentrating reductions at the beginning of the month to improve exports, which the bank did in November and December.
So far this month, the mini-band has been lowered 0.24 percent. In the last few months, the mini-band was lowered between 0.50 percent and 0.65 percent.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real fell 0.1 percent to end at 1.0468 to the dollar. In the illegal parallel market, the real rose 0.45 percent to close at 1.115 per dollar.
